observations.claim: Entering PROG creates bindings for program variables on the current a-list with NIL values.
observations.source_locator: Appendix B, The PROG Feature, item 1

observations.claim: SET/SETQ locates the variable name on the current a-list and replaces the value cell of that existing binding pair.
observations.source_locator: Appendix B, The PROG Feature, item 3

observations.claim: If the variable occurs multiple times on the a-list, only the first/most-recent occurrence is changed.
If the changed binding belongs to a higher-level scope, the new value remains effective throughout that binding's scope and the old value is lost.
If the variable is absent from the a-list, SET/SETQ signals historical A4/A5 rather than creating a fresh binding.
observations.source_locator: Appendix B, continuation of item 3; interpreter diagnostics

observations.claim: SETQ differs from SET by quoting its first argument; SET evaluates the target expression to obtain the variable name.
The value of SET/SETQ is the value of the second argument.
SET/SETQ may change variables residing on the a-list from higher-level functions.
Compiled-variable representation has additional SPECIAL/COMMON restrictions; this is a compilation caveat, not evidence against interpreter a-list update semantics.

comparison_to_2402.caveat: Historical carrier is the dynamically scoped a-list binding pair. Do not rewrite this as modern lexical-cell semantics.
